findings.title: Dangerous use of `eval()`
findings.detail: `eval()` executes arbitrary code; common RCE vector if input is untrusted.
findings.remediation: Avoid `eval`/`exec`. Use `ast.literal_eval` for data, or restructure to avoid dynamic execution.

findings.title: SQL injection risk: f-string SQL query
findings.detail: SQL string built with f-string / .format() — use parameterized queries.
findings.remediation: Use parameter substitution: `cursor.execute(sql, (param,))`.

findings.title: `pickle.loads` on untrusted input
findings.detail: `pickle.loads` allows arbitrary code execution.
findings.remediation: Use JSON or msgpack for untrusted input; never unpickle attacker-controlled bytes.

findings.title: Command injection: `shell=True` + format string
findings.detail: `shell=True` with an f-string/.format() first arg enables command injection.
findings.remediation: Use list-form subprocess (no shell) and pass arguments separately; never interpolate user input.

findings.title: TLS verification disabled (`verify=False`)
findings.detail: `verify=False` disables certificate validation. Vulnerable to MITM.
findings.remediation: Remove `verify=False`; if you must use a self-signed cert pass `verify='/path/to/cert'`.

findings.title: Weak hashing for password: `hashlib.md5`
findings.detail: MD5/SHA1 are not suitable for password hashing.
findings.remediation: Use `hashlib.bcrypt`, `argon2`, or `hashlib.scrypt`.
